Q: Which boot method uses a removable thumb drive prepared with installation media?
Option2: Optical media

Q: Which boot method uses a DVD or Blu ray disk to start the installer?
Option2: USB

Q: Which boot method starts from a server over the LAN to run an installer image?
Option2: Network

Q: Which boot method downloads install files from the vendor cloud to rebuild the OS?
Option2: Optical media

Q: Which option describes an external hot swappable drive boot?
Option1: Booting from a removable drive bay that can be attached or detached without opening the case
Option2: Only booting from CD

Q: Which option describes an internal hard drive partition boot for recovery?
Option1: A special local partition launches the recovery environment
Option2: Only a DVD can start recovery

Q: What is an in place upgrade?
Option1: Erase and install with no data migration
Option2: Install a new OS while keeping apps and user data when supported
Option3: Clone an image to many devices
Option4: Boot only to the recovery partition

Q: What is a clean install?
Option1: Install over the top to keep apps
Option2: Install a fresh OS on a new or wiped volume and then add apps and data

Q: What is image deployment?
Option2: Cloning a standardized, prebuilt OS image to target devices

Q: What is a repair installation?
Option2: Reinstall core OS files to fix problems while trying to keep data and settings

Q: What is a remote network installation?
Option2: Installation is started from a network service to target machines

Q: Why are third party drivers an installation consideration?
Option2: Storage or network controllers may need vendor drivers during setup to access disks or network
Option3: They slow the CPU by design

Q: What does partitioning do during setup?
Option2: Divides a disk into logical sections where volumes can be created

Q: Which partition table supports large disks and many partitions and is standard on modern systems?
Option2: GPT

Q: Which partition table is older and limited to about 2 TB disks and four primary partitions?
Option2: MBR

Q: What is drive format in the context of installation?
Option2: Creating a file system such as NTFS on a volume

Q: What should be done before any major upgrade?
Option2: Back up user files and preferences

Q: Which factor is an application and driver support consideration?
Option2: Confirming that critical apps and device drivers are supported on the target OS version
Option3: Number of USB ports in the case

Q: Which factor is a hardware compatibility consideration?
Option2: CPU, RAM, storage, and graphics meet the new OS minimums

Q: What are feature updates in this context?
Option2: Vendor released OS updates that add features and fixes during the product life cycle

Q: A company needs to deploy 100 identical laptops with the same corporate build quickly. Best method?
Option2: Image deployment with a standardized golden image

Option4: Use dynamic disks with MBR only

Option2: Load the storage controller driver from removable media during setup

Option2: Use staged rollout and local image or peer caching to reduce repeated WAN downloads

Option2: Solid-state/flash drive (USB) boot
